subject: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@northbridge.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity

Team —

Following our pre-sales thread with NorthBridge, they've asked for a compact delivery playbook and clear staffing commitments so procurement can finish terms. I'd like to align on the minimal "ship-able" scope for a VPC/on‑prem pilot and capture exceptions we'll need to approve. High level asks:

- Confirm minimum infra and ops responsibilities (who owns network peering, bastion/management plane, oncall windows).
- Decide whether we require a private control plane or can use a customer-managed VPC with our lightweight agent for pilot.
- Call out any non-standard security requirements that will need an exception (airgap, HSM, custom logging retention).
- Identify resource owners and a realistic staffing timeline for a 6–8 week pilot.

I've attached a draft playbook and a rough network diagram (placeholders) — please review and call out where you need more detail. Would like a short sync Thursday (Nov 25) to lock decisions so I can push to procurement.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-ops-playbook-draft.pdf (14 pages), network-diagram-v2.pptx (3 slides)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity

Naomi —

Quick notes after a skim of the draft:

- Minimal infra: 2 x GPU nodes for inference (model = 30B fp16), 1 control plane host for agent + metrics, customer-managed NAT + route table. We'll need a small bastion/management subnet for kernel updates and incident response.
- Control plane: for a pilot we can run a customer-managed VPC with our agent — that removes private control plane operational burden but requires a limited set of IAM roles and a service account.
- Exception candidates: HSM (if they insist on customer KMS), airgap (adds ~6 weeks to timeline), and enforced network egress filters that block telemetry.
- Ops burden: expect 0.25 FTE of runtime engineer for onboarding + 0.5 FTE during the pilot for support and runbook stabilization.

I'll mark up the network diagram with exact CIDR and port requirements and share by EOD. If we're comfortable with the agent model I don't think we need a full private control plane for this pilot.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal/Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity

Naomi / team —

Operational considerations from my side:

- Runbooks: we need an initial "day 0/1/30" runbook set. I can lead that, but will need 1 week of dedicated engineering time from product/runtime to write the first-pass procedures (deploy, restart, KV cache warm, failover).
- Monitoring: metrics ingestion will use our lightweight exporter to the customer's telemetry (they asked for Prometheus pushgateway); that's fine but we need permission to send only metrics (no logs) until SOC completes review.
- Oncall: propose a shared oncall rota between runtime and infra during pilot hours (9am–6pm PT), with 1 escalation to SRE after-hours if there's a cluster-level issue.
- Training: 2 x 2-hour run-through sessions for NorthBridge engineers during the first week.

I can commit to runbook ownership and the training sessions, assuming we get the 0.25–0.5 FTE runtime coverage Karthik outlined.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Manager, Customer Reliability

From: Zoe Patel <zoe.patel@northbridge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for circulating. A couple of clarifying items from procurement/security so we can correlate with our internal calendar:

- Timeline: we'd like to kick the pilot Jan 10, 2028 and expect 6 weeks. Is that feasible from your side?
- HSM/KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS for compliance — if that's an exception, please outline the impact to timeline and operations.
- Telemetry: we will accept metrics only; logs must remain on our side for 90 days. Can you confirm that the exporter can be configured to metrics-only?
- Oncall: our security team expects an oncall escalation path. Can you provide a short statement of expected response SLAs during the pilot window?

We can sign the SOW once those items are captured in the playbook. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Zoe Patel
Senior Program Manager
NorthBridge Analytics

On Wed, 24 Nov 2027 at 10:23 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> All —
> 
> Product perspective:
> 
> - Scope: for the pilot we should limit model capabilities to generation + embeddings (no retraining or data plane features). That narrows SLOs and the observability set.
> - Rollouts: we will require a canary traffic policy and a default fallback (hosted model) in case KV cache warming fails. That's a small config addition but important for SLA.
> - Acceptance criteria: defined load test (50 qps sustained, 20ms median token latency target) and a short quality check using the customer's evaluation prompts.
> 
> If we agree to the agent + customer VPC approach, product can own the acceptance tests and can run the canary config. I'll draft the acceptance checklist by Friday.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Zoe Patel <zoe.patel@northbridge.com>, procurement@northbridge.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private delivery playbook — scope decisions & resource clarity

Team / Zoe —

Thanks everyone — quick summary and decisions we'll share with procurement:

1) Pilot model & scope: generation + embeddings only. No retraining or data-plane features in pilot (Jonas to own acceptance checklist).
2) Deployment model: customer-managed VPC with Redwood agent (no private control plane for pilot). Karthik to publish exact port/CIDR matrix by EOD Wed.
3) Exceptions: customer-managed KMS/HSM is acceptable but will add ~4–6 weeks to schedule if they require hardware HSM. Airgap is out-of-scope for this pilot.
4) Ops & staffing: runtime will provide 0.25 FTE for onboarding and 0.5 FTE during pilot; Soojin will own runbooks and training sessions; product will run acceptance tests.
5) Telemetry: metrics-only exporter is acceptable — logs will remain customer-side for 90 days.
6) Oncall SLAs: pilot hours 9am–6pm PT, severity-1 response within 1 hour during pilot hours; after-hours escalation to SRE.

Action items:
- Karthik: annotated network diagram and port/CIDR matrix (due 2027-11-30 EOD).
- Jonas: acceptance checklist and load test scripts (due 2027-12-03).
- Soojin: initial runbook drafts + training schedule (due 2027-12-08).
- Naomi: update playbook with final language and send to procurement (will attach the network diagram + acceptance checklist when available).

Zoe — if this captures your asks, I'll produce a tidy playbook (v1) and a short SOW snippet for procurement to sign off.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: vpc-ops-playbook-draft.pdf, network-diagram-v2.pptx
